title: Qbar-l geometric-fiber formula
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the finite-stage pair categories $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and let $\bar y:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y P$, with projections $i_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to X$ and $a_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to P$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the scheme hypotheses of [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite-extension]: $X,Y,X_{\bar y},P$ are noetherian and finite-dimensional, $\ell$ is invertible on all four, $a_{\bar y}$ is proper, and the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at most some $e\geq0$ [def-pc-dimension]. Take the cartesian square $(f,a_{\bar y},\bar y,i_{\bar y},\mathrm{id})$ of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Use the descended direct images, pullbacks and exchange of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], from the raw rational finite-stage operations specified in [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite-extension].
For every $K\in\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ the descended exchange is an isomorphism
$$
 L\bar y^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{\bar y,*}Li_{\bar y}^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(P,\Qlb).
$$
If $K$ is represented by $(E,K_E)$, with $E\subset\Qlb$ finite over $\Ql$ and $K_E\in\Dbc(X,E)$, this morphism is represented over a finite overfield $M\subset\Qlb$ containing $E$ by the $M$-coefficient geometric-fiber exchange of [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite-extension] applied to $T_{M/E}K_E$, where $T_{M/E}$ is the scalar-extension functor of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

proof.text: In [thm-weil-pbc-qbar] substitute $Y'=P$, $X'=X_{\bar y}$, $g=\bar y$, $g'=i_{\bar y}$ and $f'=a_{\bar y}$. The chosen fiber product makes this exactly the cartesian square $(f,a_{\bar y},\bar y,i_{\bar y},\mathrm{id})$. The scheme and coefficient hypotheses are those already imposed in the statement; in particular $f$ is proper and the base-change map $g=\bar y$ is permitted because that theorem allows arbitrary $g$. Its descended exchange component therefore gives an isomorphism $L\bar y^*Rf_*K\to Ra_{\bar y,*}Li_{\bar y}^*K$ in $\Dbc(P,\Qlb)$. This is the specified exchange, rather than merely an unspecified isomorphism, since the theorem refers to the same descended exchange transformation.

proof.text: For a representative $(E,K_E)$, the representative clause of [thm-weil-pbc-qbar] supplies a finite overfield $M\supset E$ at which this very component is represented by the $M$-coefficient exchange on $T_{M/E}K_E$, with the theorem's specified comparison identifications. By [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], $T_{M/E}K_E$ belongs to $\Dbc(X,M)$. Apply [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite-extension] with coefficient field $M$ and this object: all its scheme hypotheses were imposed above, independently of the finite coefficient field. Its square is the same $(f,a_{\bar y},\bar y,i_{\bar y},\mathrm{id})$, so its displayed formula is precisely the finite-stage map supplied by the general theorem. This proves the representative clause. No passage from an etale finite-ring category to a rational category, and no identification with a condensed-coefficient category, is being asserted here.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q128-974bfa082 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the master and main-20261015 blueprint text (identical statement; one-line proof 'specialize thm-weil-pbc-qbar'), the unit and chapter records, and the statements of all cited nodes, including the blueprint_updates. Statement repair: the source's 'setup of the finite-level corollary' leaves Dbc(-,Qlb) undefined (e.g. ell=2 on Spec F_2). The added hypotheses are those of cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite-extension. Once X and Y are in the Qbar domain (noetherian, finite-dimensional, ell invertible), each one follows: a_ybar is proper by base change; X_ybar is of finite type over Omega, so noetherian and finite-dimensional; ell is invertible on P; and the fiber dimension is at most dim X, since O_{X_y,x} is a quotient of O_{X,x}. So the statement is not narrowed or weakened, and the conclusion and representative clause are verbatim. The only citer, prop-zl-smooth-proper-relative-purity, satisfies all of these hypotheses. The square (f,a_ybar,ybar,i_ybar,id) matches def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square and def-pc-fibre-product in orientation. The coefficient category is the pair category P_T of def-weil-pbc-qbar-category, with exchange descended by prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors; it is not a target, and no condensed identification is claimed. Step 1 is a literal instance of thm-weil-pbc-qbar (f proper, g arbitrary; its implicit domain is now explicit), so elementary is correct. Step 2: the representative clause of thm-weil-pbc-qbar names the M-exchange of thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension at T_{M/E}K_E, and the finite-extension corollary over M names the same exchange for the same square; this is an identification by definition. proof_deps equal the union of uses. Dropping the unused cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite edge is correct. There is no cycle, no new node and no duplicate (rg for geometric-fiber nodes found only the finite-ring and rational-E corollaries, which use other coefficients). All citations stay inside unit sk-thm-properbasechange, so no tool_uses are needed. No SGA. Edge cases checked: K=0, f=id, empty fiber, char Omega = ell excluded, M=E. No fixes.
